newsitem.title: JAPAN: IBM to license Mac OS to Japanese PC venture.
newsitem.headline: IBM to license Mac OS to Japanese PC venture.

text.p: Japanese personal computer venture Akia Corp plans to market a Macintosh clone PC as early as November in cooperation with International Business Machines Corp (IBM).
IBM Japan Ltd said on Thursday that IBM agreed at the end of August to sub-license a Mac operating system (OS) to Akia for the PC.
Since Akia does not have its own production facility, the Mac clone will be manufactured by PC peripherals maker Memorex Telex Japan Ltd.
Akia is the first firm to which IBM has sub-licensed its rights on the Mac OS, the IBM Japan spokesman said.
IBM will supply all microprocessors used in Akia's new PC, the spokesman said.

Akia also plans as early as next spring to sell a new PC based on a common hardware reference platform (CHRP), which can be installed with both Mac OS and Microsoft Corp's operating system, Windows NT.
Akia expects to post sales of 25 billion yen in its 1996/97 business year ending on June 30. Of the total, 30 percent will be from the new PC, the Akia spokesman said.
